item.title: Re: The battle of the repressed
item.content:encoded:
is the psychological improvement anomalous?

Yes, probably should have stated that.

What is the underlying narrative here, if any? If there isn’t one, how do you plan to maintain the reader’s attention through unconnected anecdotes?

This is where I found myself a bit stuck I must admit. Partly the reason for desiring to have all personnel enter as a group was so that I could allow the characters to build off of each other. In fact, I think it will serve to make the narrative better to have the characters enter as a group. I want to tell a story about the effects of a single action, how one action can cause a domino effect. And also a story about a group of characters coming to terms with their trauma. Perhaps changing it so you do not *need* to kill the manifestations will make the characters psychological improvements seem more genuine? Perhaps even raise the question to if it is an anomalous property? Instead, the characters need to overcome flaws such as a cowardly D-Class finally standing up for themselves and the group causes their manifested trauma weaker or appear less.

Alright, here’s my take.

In general, 'Maniac'-style anomalies can be useful for story-telling. I do, however, have some concerns.

To start, is the psychological improvement anomalous? If not, I don’t see how these events would help the anomaly’s victims in any way. The first D-Class, for instance, probably wouldn’t garner an improved mental state from murdering a mangled version of itself.

In addition, I’m not currently seeing any connection between your planned subjects/foci. What is the underlying narrative here, if any? If there isn’t one, how do you plan to maintain the reader’s attention through unconnected anecdotes?


If you respond to this comment and would like me to see it, please send me a Wikidot PM, as I will not be notified otherwise.

item.title: Re: The battle of the repressed
item.content:encoded:
I’m noticing you’re getting very vague when it gets to the hook. You hadn’t mentioned trusting the being or the characters being connected before now.

Haha yep, I really could have presented that sooner.

I do have to question the exploration log in general. Are these people who were sent into the building or did they go in on their own accord? Even if the Foundation would be willing to send people into a dangerous SCP, why are they writing a log while running from inner trauma?

The people are sent in. I worded myself badly; I meant a video log, like a camera given to the people to record the interior of the SCP.

I feel that maybe having the characters interact with each other would help make the story more enjoyable? Mixing inner problems with outer problems, so to speak. It would make the connection between the people easier to integrate and occur more organically?

Overall, I think the people can make or break this thing. The idea has so many directions it can go in that it matters most who you put in and how they respond. You seem to have gotten the who you put in part, now I’m just curious how they respond.

This is the hardest part, I'm going to spend some time brainstorming and outlining how to have the characters respond to everything that happens. Thank you for your crit, I found it very insightful :)

item.title: Re: The battle of the repressed
item.content:encoded:
I’d say the concept itself has merit, I’m reminded of many Saw-esque horror movies where characters go though trauma to better themselves psychologically. That’s not to say the idea’s overdone, you just need to make sure you’re doing it right.

I’m noticing you’re getting very vague when it gets to the hook. You hadn’t mentioned trusting the being or the characters being connected before now. I can understand the religion and cult being connected, but I need a bit more of an explanation for the rest. Even if they are, I’m not sure if you should do them all in the same log. Unless you want to have their battles directly overlap, because I don’t know how you would have four completely independent narratives in one exploration log.

I do have to question the exploration log in general. Are these people who were sent into the building or did they go in on their own accord? Even if the Foundation would be willing to send people into a dangerous SCP, why are they writing a log while running from inner trauma? I would wonder if an interview would work better. That way not only is it done after the fact but it also shows their perspective on their inner trauma. That might also fix the fact that I wasn’t really seeing a conclusion. You just have four exploration logs and then it’s done. Maybe the idea you touched on in the hook is what you’re using for your ending, but I don’t really know what that is.

Overall, I think the people can make or break this thing. The idea has so many directions it can go in that it matters most who you put in and how they respond. You seem to have gotten the who you put in part, now I’m just curious how they respond.

item.title: The battle of the repressed
item.content:encoded:
Been a good while since I last tried to write on here. Feel free to tear this idea to shreds ^_^

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Emotional

Elevator Pitch: A small building with an interior that varies in size and form based on what individual enters. Additionally, the individual's traumas and/or regrets will manifest, needing to be killed in order for the individual to leave. If the individual is successful they will immediately improve psychologically despite their ordeal within the building. Following 5 hours after leaving, the individual forgets the experience, but retain the psychological benefits.

Central Narrative:

Open me!
I am open

The stories of 4 individuals overcoming various internal conflicts through the SCP. Done through exploration logs and interviews.

A D-Class that had killed an innocent man for his girlfriend finds himself fighting a succubus and a version of themselves fused with multiple weapons.

A former researcher now turned D-Class scared to leave their religion enters the SCP willingly. They enter into a church that leads to a hellscape. A grotesquely muscular version of their mother dressed in a nun outfit pursues them.

A demoted MTF member that killed his squad to prevent a cognitohazard from spreading finds himself inside a dark complex. A hovering humanoid with a cloud-like mass of tendrils and small humanoids for a head chasses after him. The small humanoids accuse the MTF of being a murderer.

A D-Class suffering immense paranoia due to being raised by a cultist family that believed all who were not a part of their religion were demonic beings. They enter into an endless, dark, room. A being that is best described as eldritch follows after them. It calls out to the D-Class, claiming it wants to help them escape.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story of the paranoid D-Class turns the SCP on its head. As instead of killing, they must trust the being, showing there may be more to the SCP. Also, all the characters are connected, each having contributed to each others trauma.

Additional Notes: Should I combine all the stories into one log? With the four subjects entering as a group? Would it be a better idea to change it from "killing your trauma" to something else? Also, apologies for any sloppy writing, I'm tired.

Edit: Considering making the SCP more nuanced.
